classification.difficultyReason: Compare angle sums in two nested triangles using a common angle and the given equality.

content.prompt: In the figure below, $\angle B=\angle 1$. Prove that $\angle A=\angle 2$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with an internal segment joining unlabelled points on BC and AC. Labels 1 and 2 lie inside the smaller triangle adjacent to the internal segment. Source has no angle arcs, shading or equal-length marks.
spec.mathematics: A, Q and C are collinear; B, P and C are collinear. Angle 1 is PQC and angle 2 is QPC. Both triangles share the angle at C.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original vertex and angle labels are visible; no proof or answer is drawn.

answer.short:
$\angle A=\angle 2$.

Both triangles share $\angle C$ and have equal remaining angles $\angle B=\angle 1$, so their third angles are equal.
answer.worked:
Apply the angle sum to the large triangle and the smaller triangle. They share $\angle C$, and $\angle B=\angle 1$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle A&=180^{\circ}-\angle B-\angle C\\\angle A&=180^{\circ}-\angle 1-\angle C\\\angle A&=\angle 2.\end{align*}$$
